primitives.name: Cold-Start Consolidation Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Why they are needed, in one line each.** | Route | Why | |---|---| | `GET /api/mobile/v1/bootstrap` | One cold-start call instead of four.
primitives.assumptions: Client performs initial sync with minimal network overhead; all dependent data is fetched in one round-trip.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When TLS handshakes exceed cellular latency threshold, performance degrades linearly with number of endpoints.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's loadBoardState and getUserEntitlements functions, ensuring consistent data flow between client and backend services.
layer2.telemetry: Network round-trip time (RTT) and TLS handshake duration

primitives.name: Native Authentication Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: | | `POST /api/mobile/v1/auth/exchange` | A native client cannot use a NextAuth cookie session.
primitives.assumptions: Web-based authentication is prerequisite for native session validity; token generation requires prior successful login flow.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when web sign-in process does not complete before token request, resulting in unauthorized access denial.

layer2.mapping: Derives from GSI's session management logic, adapted for mobile context with explicit bearer token issuance.
layer2.telemetry: Token issuance success rate and authentication error codes

primitives.name: In-App Purchase Validator
primitives.verbatim_quote: | | `POST /api/mobile/v1/receipts` | Verifies a StoreKit 2 JWS and grants the tier.
primitives.assumptions: Receipt validation ensures cryptographic integrity of purchase claims; Apple root CA is required for certificate chain verification.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If Apple root CA PEM is absent, service returns 503, halting all entitlement updates until resolution.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors GSI's entitlement filtering mechanism but applied specifically to iOS in-app purchase lifecycle.
layer2.telemetry: Receipt signature verification status and tier assignment accuracy
